title: Tirzepatide (a diabetes and weight-loss injection) for active central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia: a 20-person pilot now recruiting
headline: A repurposing idea: a 12-month, single-arm pilot of weekly tirzepatide in adults with active CCCA, started September 2026, with paired scalp biopsies; it enrols people with higher HbA1c and insulin resistance, and results are years away.
evidenceTier: Registry record read in full (ClinicalTrials.gov); a 2026 meta-analysis abstract is the only supporting data (abstract read)
fit: Relevant only to confirmed, active CCCA and only as a specialist prescription decision. It does link to this run's insulin-resistance theme, but nothing here supports self-directed use.
displaces: Fits nowhere in a routine; it would be a specialist-led addition or replacement in CCCA treatment.
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
summaryPoints: Registry record (read in full): NCT07734870; Johns Hopkins with Eli Lilly collaborating; 20 adults with active CCCA (activity score above 1), weekly tirzepatide for 12 months, no control arm; scalp biopsies at baseline and 6 months with RNA sequencing of scarring pathways; started 15 September 2026, completion expected May 2028.
Eligibility excludes HbA1c below 5.4% and HOMA-IR below 2, so it enrols people who already have some metabolic burden; it also excludes people already on glucose-lowering or weight-loss drugs.

Context (abstract read): a 2026 meta-analysis of GLP-1 drugs and hair loss found about a 40% higher risk of non-scarring hair loss (telogen effluvium and androgenetic alopecia), and reports that 58% of people with CCCA improved on these drugs; I did not open the primary data for that figure.
Watch re-check: the baricitinib CCCA phase 2 from the earlier run is still completed with no results posted and no publication found.
toneData: Condition-specific: CCCA mainly affects women of African descent (background; the record does not restrict by ancestry)
fitLine: Condition- and prescription-specific; a pilot with no control arm.

fitAxes.why: Not applicable to a systemic drug.
